public_rationale: The arithmetic is right: 29,000 hours a month spread over about 1,500 engineers is about 19 hours each. But both inputs come only from the speaker's reading of an internal Zillow deck that is not public. I found no Zillow disclosure or independent report that confirms the reviewer-load figure, the headcount, or that the added load is all review of AI-written code. Zillow's own June 2026 post confirms humans review AI output before it merges but gives no numbers. Without the deck or another primary source, the claim can be neither confirmed nor refuted.
limitations: The only source for the key figures is the speaker, whose writing cannot be used as evidence.
Absence of corroboration is not evidence the figures are wrong.

The month or period the deck measured is not stated. The period is set to January 1 through May 19, 2026 (the months before the post) and flagged. It is not limited to April.
criteria.support_condition: Zillow's deck or another independent source shows added reviewer load of roughly 29,000 hours a month and an engineering headcount of about 1,500, about 19 hours per engineer, tied to AI-generated code.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Zillow's own figures show a materially different added review load or engineering headcount, or show that the added load is not tied to AI-generated output.
